verdicts.label: pass
verdicts.meaning: Every check in scope ran on trustworthy evidence and nothing blocks.

verdicts.label: pass, conditionally
verdicts.meaning: Nothing blocks, but the pass rests on named conditions (default rules, guessed or fallback models, partly modelled parts, inferred pin roles, parts with no model, checks that could not judge a part or did not run); each condition says how to lift it.

verdicts.label: fail
verdicts.meaning: At least one blocking finding or failed assertion.

verdicts.label: partly judged, not a pass
verdicts.meaning: Nothing blocks among the checks that ran, but key parts have no usable model, so the checks they could change were not judged.

verdicts.label: inconclusive, not a pass
verdicts.meaning: The run's own evidence is not trustworthy (a refusal, an undermined claim, a failed simulation), so it vouches for nothing either way.

evidence_grades.label: full evidence
evidence_grades.meaning: The conclusion stands on evidence alone: nothing on its causal path was assumed.

evidence_grades.label: qualified evidence
evidence_grades.meaning: The conclusion holds with named caveats: assumptions sit on its path, none critical.

evidence_grades.label: undermined evidence
evidence_grades.meaning: A critical assumption sits on the causal path, so the conclusion gets no verdict.

severities.label: serious
severities.meaning: A real problem with the design.

blocking.label: blocking
blocking.meaning: The gate fails the run on this finding unless it is waived. Independent of severity: a gating warning blocks.

exit_codes.label: fail
exit_codes.meaning: Fail: a blocking finding or a failed assertion.

exit_codes.label: usage or input error
exit_codes.meaning: Usage, spec or input error: the run did not start.

exit_codes.label: not judged
exit_codes.meaning: Partly judged or inconclusive: not a pass, and not a fail.

exit_codes.label: tool fault
exit_codes.meaning: Internal error in hauksbee itself; please report it.

checks.label: Design rules (DRC)
checks.meaning: Copper geometry against the clearance and width rules: shorts, spacing, unrouted pads.

checks.label: Connectivity lint
checks.meaning: The netlist the copper implements: floating inputs, unpowered parts, wrong values.

checks.label: Signal integrity
checks.meaning: Signal integrity of fast nets: impedance, length and coupling.

checks.label: MCU resources
checks.meaning: MCU pins and peripherals the board uses, against what the part provides.

checks.label: USB-C
checks.meaning: USB-C configuration: CC resistors, VBUS and the receptacle wiring.

checks.label: Thermal
checks.meaning: Dissipation and temperature rise of each part against its ratings.

checks.label: AC response
checks.meaning: Small-signal frequency response of the solved circuit.

checks.label: Firmware co-simulation
checks.meaning: Compiled firmware run against the solved board, with ratings checked over time.

checks.label: Spec assertions
checks.meaning: The assertions a hauksbee-ci spec states, each judged against the run.

checks.label: Evidence
checks.meaning: Claims whose own evidence is undermined, reported as findings.

glossary.label: PASS
glossary.short: The check held, and nothing it depends on had to be guessed.
glossary.what_to_do: Nothing. Keep the check so a later change that breaks it is caught.

glossary.label: FAIL
glossary.short: The board was simulated and the check did not hold. This is a finding about your design.
glossary.what_to_do: Read the reason under the check: it names the net or part and what was seen. Fix the design (or the limit, if the limit is wrong) and rerun.

glossary.label: PARTLY JUDGED / INCONCLUSIVE
glossary.short: Hauksbee refused to give this a pass or fail, because something it rests on was not simulated (an open part, an unpowered regulator, firmware that never ran). It is not a failure of your board.
glossary.what_to_do: Close the named gap and rerun.

glossary.label: Conditional pass
glossary.short: Passed, but only under the assumptions listed.
glossary.what_to_do: Each assumption names what would make the pass unconditional.

glossary.label: Open part
glossary.short: A part with no model. It is left out of the circuit (treated as not there), so readings on its nets show the board without it.
glossary.what_to_do: Give it a model (draft one from its datasheet), or mark it DNP if the board does not fit it.

glossary.label: Stand-in model
glossary.short: No model matched this exact part, so a similar one stood in. Where the two differ, results describe the stand-in.
glossary.what_to_do: Add a model for the real part, or name the exact part fitted.

glossary.label: Reduced fidelity
glossary.short: This part or result was simulated with a simpler stand-in. It is good enough for the claim shown, but not for finer ones.
glossary.what_to_do: Usually nothing. To tighten it, give the run what the entry asks for.

glossary.label: Assumed corner
glossary.short: The board names only the kind of part (e.g. 'LED'), so Hauksbee checked a high and a low plausible part.
glossary.what_to_do: Put the real part number on it to check that part instead.

glossary.label: Not exercised
glossary.short: The run never reached this (a regulator with no input supply, a bus never addressed, firmware that never ran), so there is no result for it.
glossary.what_to_do: Supply what the entry names (a supply, firmware, a stimulus) and rerun.

glossary.label: Not checked
glossary.short: This check could not run on these inputs. No findings here does not mean there are none.
glossary.what_to_do: Give the run the input the entry names and rerun.

glossary.label: Inferred pin role
glossary.short: Nothing said what this pin does, so Hauksbee went by the usual pin order for the package.
glossary.what_to_do: If that is wrong for this part, name the pin roles in its model.

glossary.label: Default value
glossary.short: A value the inputs did not give was set to a documented default.
glossary.what_to_do: Set the real value in the part's model or in the spec.

glossary.label: Assumed fitted
glossary.short: With no BOM, every placed part is treated as fitted, including any left off the real board.
glossary.what_to_do: Supply a BOM that marks the parts that are not fitted.

glossary.label: Outside part limits
glossary.short: The run measured a part outside a limit its datasheet sets, so results that depend on it are not trusted.
glossary.what_to_do: Bring the part inside the named limit (change the circuit or the part).

glossary.label: Reader limitation
glossary.short: The file reader has a known gap here, so findings in this area may be missing or wrong.
glossary.what_to_do: Re-export from a supported tool version, or confirm these findings by hand.

glossary.label: Waived
glossary.short: Someone accepted this finding by hand, with a reason and an end date. It does not fail the run until that date.
glossary.what_to_do: Fix the finding before the waiver ends, or renew it with a fresh reason.

glossary.label: Default rules
glossary.short: The board's own spacing and width rules were not available, so checks used Hauksbee's defaults.
glossary.what_to_do: Put the project's .kicad_pro next to the board so its own rules are used.

glossary.label: Identity only
glossary.short: Hauksbee knows the part and its pins, but not what it does, so it stays open in simulation.
glossary.what_to_do: Give its model behaviour (draft it from the datasheet) to simulate it.

glossary.label: Partly modelled
glossary.short: The part simulates, but only some of what it does is modelled.
glossary.what_to_do: Results that need the rest are not evidence; extend the model to cover them.

glossary.label: Coverage not listed
glossary.short: The part simulates, but its model does not list which behaviours it covers, so Hauksbee cannot tell which results it vouches for.
glossary.what_to_do: Add the behaviours the model covers to its coverage list (open it in the model editor), so the results it supports can count.

glossary.label: Report only
glossary.short: This command reports problems but still exits 0, so a script or CI job will not fail on them.
glossary.what_to_do: Add --strict to make serious findings fail the build.

glossary.label: Halted
glossary.short: The emulated microcontroller is not executing firmware right now: the simulation is paused, the firmware has stopped (a fault, a sleep it never wakes from, or the end of main), or its supply is below the operating range.
glossary.what_to_do: Press play; if it stays halted while the sim runs, check the MCU's supply rail and the serial output for a crash message.

glossary.label: UART traffic
glossary.short: The microcontroller sent or received bytes on its serial port (UART) in the last two seconds of real time; the console shows what it printed.
glossary.what_to_do: Open the Serial tab to read the output or type input to the firmware.

entries.explain: Nothing blocks among the checks that ran, but key parts have no usable model, so the checks they could change were not judged.

entries.label: inconclusive, not a pass
entries.explain: The run's own evidence is not trustworthy (a refusal, an undermined claim, a failed simulation), so it vouches for nothing either way.

entries.label: full evidence
entries.explain: The conclusion stands on evidence alone: nothing on its causal path was assumed.

entries.label: qualified evidence
entries.explain: The conclusion holds with named caveats: assumptions sit on its path, none critical.

entries.label: undermined evidence
entries.explain: A critical assumption sits on the causal path, so the conclusion gets no verdict.

entries.label: Design rules (DRC)
entries.explain: Copper geometry against the clearance and width rules: shorts, spacing, unrouted pads.

entries.label: Connectivity lint
entries.explain: The netlist the copper implements: floating inputs, unpowered parts, wrong values.

entries.label: Signal integrity
entries.explain: Signal integrity of fast nets: impedance, length and coupling.

entries.label: MCU resources
entries.explain: MCU pins and peripherals the board uses, against what the part provides.

entries.label: USB-C
entries.explain: USB-C configuration: CC resistors, VBUS and the receptacle wiring.

entries.label: Thermal
entries.explain: Dissipation and temperature rise of each part against its ratings.

entries.label: AC response
entries.explain: Small-signal frequency response of the solved circuit.

entries.label: Firmware co-simulation
entries.explain: Compiled firmware run against the solved board, with ratings checked over time.

entries.label: Spec assertions
entries.explain: The assertions a hauksbee-ci spec states, each judged against the run.

entries.label: Evidence
entries.explain: Claims whose own evidence is undermined, reported as findings.

entries.label: PARTLY JUDGED / INCONCLUSIVE
entries.explain: Hauksbee refused to give this a pass or fail, because something it rests on was not simulated (an open part, an unpowered regulator, firmware that never ran). It is not a failure of your board.

entries.label: Conditional pass
entries.explain: Passed, but only under the assumptions listed.

entries.label: Open part
entries.explain: A part with no model. It is left out of the circuit (treated as not there), so readings on its nets show the board without it.

entries.label: Stand-in model
entries.explain: No model matched this exact part, so a similar one stood in. Where the two differ, results describe the stand-in.

entries.label: Reduced fidelity
entries.explain: This part or result was simulated with a simpler stand-in. It is good enough for the claim shown, but not for finer ones.

entries.label: Assumed corner
entries.explain: The board names only the kind of part (e.g. 'LED'), so Hauksbee checked a high and a low plausible part.

entries.label: Not exercised
entries.explain: The run never reached this (a regulator with no input supply, a bus never addressed, firmware that never ran), so there is no result for it.

entries.label: Not checked
entries.explain: This check could not run on these inputs. No findings here does not mean there are none.

entries.label: Inferred pin role
entries.explain: Nothing said what this pin does, so Hauksbee went by the usual pin order for the package.

entries.label: Default value
entries.explain: A value the inputs did not give was set to a documented default.

entries.label: Assumed fitted
entries.explain: With no BOM, every placed part is treated as fitted, including any left off the real board.

entries.label: Outside part limits
entries.explain: The run measured a part outside a limit its datasheet sets, so results that depend on it are not trusted.

entries.label: Reader limitation
entries.explain: The file reader has a known gap here, so findings in this area may be missing or wrong.

entries.label: Waived
entries.explain: Someone accepted this finding by hand, with a reason and an end date. It does not fail the run until that date.

entries.label: Default rules
entries.explain: The board's own spacing and width rules were not available, so checks used Hauksbee's defaults.

entries.label: Coverage not listed
entries.explain: The part simulates, but its model does not list which behaviours it covers, so Hauksbee cannot tell which results it vouches for.

entries.label: Report only
entries.explain: This command reports problems but still exits 0, so a script or CI job will not fail on them.

entries.label: Halted
entries.explain: The emulated microcontroller is not executing firmware right now: the simulation is paused, the firmware has stopped (a fault, a sleep it never wakes from, or the end of main), or its supply is below the operating range.

entries.label: UART traffic
entries.explain: The microcontroller sent or received bytes on its serial port (UART) in the last two seconds of real time; the console shows what it printed.
